content.summary: When a diagnosis is not established following coronary angiography, MINOCA is a working (not final) diagnosis. Clinicians should perform further assessments to establish the underlying cause so a final diagnosis and appropriate management can be made; failure to identify the cause may lead to inadequate or inappropriate therapy.
content.recommended_definitive_test: ICA (invasive coronary angiography) is the recommended definitive diagnostic test for ACS patients.
further_evaluation_recommendations: If MINOCA cause not established with ICA alone, consider left ventriculography (including measurement of LV end-diastolic pressure), functional assessment of microvascular function/coronary reactivity, and intravascular imaging.
Use adjunctive tests (termed 'functional coronary angiography') such as testing for coronary microvascular dysfunction and vasoreactivity.

figure.title: The MINOCA diagnostic algorithm
figure.figure_caption: Figure 16. Evaluation of patients with a working diagnosis of MINOCA.

Step 1 - Cath lab assessment: Detailed angiographic assessment ± LV angiography (including LV end-diastolic pressure)
Assess for coronary microvascular dysfunction ± vasoreactivity (ACh testing)

key_terms_and_abbreviations.MINOCA: myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (working diagnosis)
